bearings.paper_claim: RATE/TOC tests whether a ranking sorts units by treatment effect. In the Brazil RCT (n about 17,000 students, 850 schools), ranking by low financial autonomy gave AUTOC 0.69 (SE 0.22, t about 3.2). Ranking by out-of-bag forest CATE gave one-sided p = 0.65 (the text says this rejects, which the printed p-value does not). Qini curves for budgeted targeting and depth-1 policy trees from doubly robust scores are described (pp.7-10).
bearings.paper_location: pp.7-10 (BLP, OOB AUTOC p=0.65, autonomy TOC 0.69, policy_tree split at 41); Qini in guided tour via maq (not run)
bearings.system_side: Untapped potential (untapped.py docstring): undecided = (1 - |2s-1|) x t; supporter = s x (1-t); potential = (wp x undecided + (1-wp) x supporter) x (1 + wi x i), with s candidate support, t turnout, i sphere percentile. wp and wi come from the district settings (module default 0.5, 0.5). The score is a fixed formula with no effect-heterogeneity estimate and no RATE or Qini check.

bearings.transfer_conditions: Needs randomized or known-propensity knock vs no-knock assignment with logged outcomes (support ID or validated turnout), scored as RATE on held-out doors. Without randomized contacts, any test is an observational CATE that assumes unconfoundedness. Not transferable from this tutorial as evidence about the formula.
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers and method description verified against the text. Corrections: the p = 0.65 result does not reject (text wording is wrong); wp = 0.5 is only the module default, not the district value; line cite is 8-9. The claim that the formula presumes effects peak at s = 0.5 is an interpretation of the formula, not something the code states; reworded in paper_claim and system_side.

bearings.paper_claim: Effect heterogeneity is tested by ranking on a score and computing the gain over the ATE in the top-ranked fraction (TOC/AUTOC), which requires treated and untreated units. The authors warn that out-of-bag TOC is a heuristic without finite-sample guarantees and that policy trees need a held-out set (pp.8-11).
bearings.paper_location: pp.8-11 (OOB heuristic p.8; policy tree held-out note p.10; poverty example evaluated on held-out test sample p.11)
bearings.system_side: H1 in the prospective-contract protocol: frozen seed_prob correlates positively with new cosponsorships adopted after the freeze (Spearman over members with panel coverage in both snapshots). This is an association with the outcome level, not a test of whether contact moves high-seed_prob members more.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Effect-modification reading applies only if CU outreach or money exposure is logged per member with plausibly known assignment. Otherwise H1 is a predictive-validity check. The held-out, single-look design is consistent with the authors' advice, but this is a judgment, not something the paper tests.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claims about RATE needing treated and untreated units, the OOB heuristic caveat and held-out advice are in the text. The H1 description matches code line 17 (PROTOCOL_TEXT starts there). Rel's characterization of H1 as predictive rather than effect-modification is a fair reading of the code.

summary_issues: Summary's whole-sample AUTOC p = 0.65 is the right number, but the vignette text says the one-sided test rejects the null. A pnorm upper-tail p of 0.65 does not reject, so the vignette's wording is wrong and should not be repeated.

Flags call the 0.69 autonomy AUTOC a same-sample out-of-bag heuristic. The text does not say that. The autonomy covariate was chosen after the BLP result (p = 0.0099) on the same data, with no held-out set or selection adjustment. It is post-selected in-sample evidence, and the summary should say so.
The poverty AUTOC is described as held-out (correct: text evaluates on the 40 percent test sample, p.11). The 0.0061 SE 0.0092 t 0.67 figures match.
Summary calls the BLP terms null. Cash-transfer p = 0.066 is nominally significant at 10 percent; say 'not significant at 5 percent' instead.
Untapped code_ref cites lines 9-10; the formula sits in the docstring at lines 8-9. wp = 0.5 is only DEFAULT_WEIGHTS for districts without a setting, not the district value.
Summary says PERS is an inverted-U table; the values do not form a clean U. The 533-member count and the 'about 60 percent of cells' for the 0.45 default were not verified.
